direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt requires a pure Rust 2021 Cargo project, root test14.rs, std-only modules, exact CLI parsing, exact output formatting, and black-box behavior matching the reference binary.
The cell aggregate reports parallel mode, actual parallel use, two subagents, successful artifact capture, and a 40/40 completed quality result.
The completed official status confirms parallel mode, one AgentSwarm call with two child ids, valid protocol, artifact files, and evaluation solution_passed true.
The official evaluator summary completed successfully and reports 40 of 40 evaluated testcases passed with solution_passed true.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level server journal for the parallel session; it records session creation, tool calls, background task termination, and prompt completion without additional semantic actor content beyond the projected wire streams.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace session directory and confirms the working directory used by the run.
Implementation child received the Rust port assignment, wrote Cargo.toml, immer.rs, and test14.rs, compiled with cargo and rustc, and verified the specified nonnegative/default reference cases.
Probe child characterized the C++ reference over nonnegative, negative, partial-parse, invalid, overflow, multiple-argument, and large-input cases, returning a detailed behavior table.

Parallel parent checked toolchain, spawned the two child scopes, consumed both reports, inspected child-written files, edited the entry parser and negative behavior, stopped a pathological large-case check, optimized push_back, reran a broad matrix, and delivered the final summary.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires std-only Rust, root test14.rs, Cargo support, exact CLI behavior, exact output formatting, and black-box reference matching.
The cell aggregate reports serial mode, no parallel use, no subagents, successful artifact capture, and a completed 38/40 quality result.
The completed official status confirms serial mode, no delegation, artifact files, and evaluation solution_passed false with 38 of 40 testcases passed.
The official evaluator summary completed successfully and reports 38 of 40 evaluated testcases passed with solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level server journal for the serial session; it records one main agent turn, direct writes, local checks, and completion without any subagent or delegation activity.
Session index maps the serial session id to the workspace session directory and confirms the working directory used by the run.
The serial main actor wrote the Cargo project directly, used Rust parse() in test14.rs, verified n=0..5,14,100 and default plus one cargo case, and then reported completion.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and child briefs tracked the root Cargo project, root test14.rs entry, std-only implementation, exact output including the n=0 empty line, C++ size_t loop behavior, std::stoi-style parsing, and broad reference-byte comparison obligations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned coordination and final repair. It delegated implementation to agent-0 and read-only reference probing to agent-1, then resumed direct ownership of integration, edge-case fixes, performance repair, and final verification.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote the initial Cargo.toml, immer.rs, and test14.rs. After receiving the probe, the parent edited test14.rs to emulate std::stoi abort/out_of_range and negative-index reference behavior, then edited immer.rs so push_back consumed self and used Rc::make_mut for large-input performance.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation child was the only child writer, the probe child used /tmp only, and the parent integrated by editing the existing files after child completion. The final artifact list contains Cargo.toml, test14.rs, immer.rs, and built binaries.
parallel.verification: The run first verified the child implementation against n=0,1,2,3,4,5,14,20 and no-arg, then the parent reran cargo/rustc and a broader byte/exit-code matrix including negatives, partial parses, overflow, 100000, and 1000000 with fail=0.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved task gap is visible at closure; the official evaluator completed and passed all 40 of 40 testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the root Cargo project, module organization, root test14.rs, std-only code, default n=14, n=0 loop underflow behavior, and byte-for-byte checking for representative visible cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main actor owned the full task end to end, writing Cargo.toml, immer_vector.rs, and test14.rs directly without subagents or separate probing.
serial.implementation: The serial test14.rs used args[1].parse().expect for CLI parsing and cast n/2 to usize for indexing. That matched basic integer inputs but did not implement C++ std::stoi partial parsing, leading whitespace, overflow abort parity, or all negative-index behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run produced a coherent Cargo project with root test14.rs and a module file, and cargo built successfully. There were no shared-state merges or child handoffs.
serial.verification: The serial checks compared rustc output for n=0,1,2,3,4,5,14,100 and default, then ran cargo build and compared only n=3 from the cargo binary.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed but marked the serial solution false at 38/40, consistent with uncovered CLI/edge behavior not exercised by the serial verification matrix.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel tracked the explicit task requirements and added reference-derived edge requirements for partial std::stoi parsing, overflow aborts, negative n behavior, and large n performance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial tracked the explicit visible requirements and sample outputs but did not surface the hidden edge behavior beyond the provided n=0 examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel expanded the behavioral contract through a dedicated black-box probe, while serial treated ordinary Rust integer parsing and the sample matrix as sufficient.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned implementation to agent-0 and reference probing to agent-1, with the main actor retaining final integration and repair ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept the entire implementation, checking, and final response in one main actor with no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained an independent behavioral probe without losing final ownership; serial had less coordination overhead but also less independent coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child briefs separated write ownership from read-only probing and included the key output, parsing, build, and verification constraints; the returned prober findings were specific enough for the parent to apply.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff interfaces, but the single actor's local model of CLI parsing stayed narrower than the prompt's exact C++ behavior requirement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's handoff moved useful reference behavior to the parent, while serial never generated an equivalent interface or behavioral spec for edge parsing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel started from the child implementation, then parent edits replaced the parser with a std::stoi emulation and added explicit negative/overflow behavior and an optimized persistent-vector push.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a simpler Vec-backed vector and entry file using args[1].parse().expect plus direct usize casts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation difference is concrete: parallel translated the C++ parsing and edge-case behavior, while serial kept Rust's stricter parse and panic behavior for some inputs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both child results returned through the AgentSwarm result, and the parent explicitly inspected files and consumed the probe before additional edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its local writes and tests flowed directly to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose child work; the useful prober handoff was received and acted on, unlike a missing-join or unused-result episode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the implementation child wrote /output during the swarm; the probe child used scratch space and the parent edited after child completion, so the final files had a clear integration path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial directly wrote all project files in a single actor, so no merge or shared workspace coordination was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more actors but no observed write collision or provenance ambiguity; serial's single-owner path was simpler but less complete behaviorally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed initial visible-case diffs, then final cargo/rustc checks over nonnegative, negative, partial parse, overflow, large, and default inputs with fail=0; official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified rustc for n=0,1,2,3,4,5,14,100 and default, then cargo for n=3 only; official evaluation later passed 38/40 and failed the solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive difference is verification breadth: parallel verified the edge cases that drove parser and negative-behavior fixes, while serial closed after a narrower matrix.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and tokens, and one overlarge validation command was killed, but the parent used the event to optimize push_back and still closed normally with complete official success.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished quickly with far fewer requests and no timeout, but it closed before discovering two failing official cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's larger budget bought edge-case coverage and final correctness; serial's shorter path left ordinary behavioral gaps rather than a coordination failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Parallel passed and serial failed because the parallel parent used a separate probing child to discover exact C++ reference behavior beyond the visible examples, then converted that information into code fixes and a wider byte/exit-code verification matrix. The serial solution was coherent for visible nonnegative cases but used Rust parse() and direct usize indexing for negative midpoints, then stopped after limited tests; the official evaluator reports 38/40 rather than a full pass.
parallel_contributors: A dedicated probe child characterized partial std::stoi parsing, whitespace, overflow aborts, negative n behavior, multiple args, and large n performance.
The parent consumed that probe, edited the parser and negative behavior, fixed O(n^2) push_back performance after a killed large-case check, and reran a broad matrix with fail=0.
serial_contributors: The serial code used args[1].parse().expect rather than std::stoi-like prefix parsing and abort classification.
The serial verification matrix omitted partial parse, leading whitespace, invalid/overflow exit parity, and negative-index reference behavior before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's strict Rust parse() was an ordinary implementation mismatch with the C++ CLI contract.
Serial did not implement the deterministic negative n reference behavior for n <= -2; it would cast a negative midpoint to a huge usize and index the Vec.
evaluator_effects: The available status summaries do not list the exact two failed official cases, so the hidden-case mapping is inferred from implementation and verification evidence rather than per-case evaluator logs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicit: agent-0 was assigned to create the Cargo project and the parent later owned repairs and final verification.
There were not separately implemented components needing unowned interface reconciliation; the parent inspected and integrated the child output directly.
Assembly and delivery were owned and completed: the parent delivered Cargo.toml, root test14.rs, module code, and built binaries.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from child reports through edits, build checks, expanded verification, and final response.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the implementation child wrote files while the probe child independently characterized behavior.
The investigation did not consume a separate first phase before implementation; probing and implementation were launched together and both completed before parent repair.
No indispensable implementation path was starved; the parent had time to consume results, edit code, optimize performance, and verify successfully.
The two-child fan-out did not exhaust budget or leave final work unfinished; the completed official evaluation passed all 40 cases.
No child was left with an overbroad unfinished assignment; agent-0 completed implementation and agent-1 completed probing, and parent follow-up was routine integration.

The implementation child brief included the known task, environment, entry-file, parsing, output-format, n=0, build, and reference-comparison requirements; extra negative/overflow behavior came from a separate probe and was not lost.

The two child scopes did not produce independently owned interoperating components; one wrote the project and the other reported reference behavior, so no missing API/file contract caused incompatibility.
The needed probe findings did not disappear in transfer; the parent explicitly referenced the negative and stoi gaps and edited code from that information.
Although the probe report was long, it was structured into cases and conclusions and the parent successfully reduced it into concrete edits and tests.
No child or parent acted on a superseded workspace or requirement state; the parent inspected the current files before applying probe-driven edits.
The child reports were compatible: implementation provided a working baseline and probing identified additional behavior, with no unresolved conflicting contract.
The parent did not accept completion from file existence or component checks alone; after edits it ran a broad byte/exit-code matrix and the official evaluator passed.
No replacement child or retry repeated earlier work without inherited checkpoints; the parent made targeted edits based on accumulated findings.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child agent was stopped before returning needed work; the only explicit stop was a local background Bash check after child completion.
A complete candidate was promoted and verified before closure; no directly promotable final artifact was left unplaced or unbuilt at the end.
The parent performed edits after initial checks but reran the broader cargo/rustc and reference-comparison matrix after those edits.
The implementation child's files were present and inspected by the parent, then the parent edited and used them for final delivery.
The probing verifier's findings returned in the AgentSwarm result and were visible to the parent before final edits and verification.
When the parent saw edge gaps and the pathological large-case command, it took over with targeted code fixes and a performance correction before closure.
The completed probe result was not ignored; the parent summarized its negative/stoi findings, inspected the code, and applied corresponding edits.
The parent did not wait blindly to timeout; it stopped a problematic background check after observing the issue and corrected the implementation.
No competing component designs needed reconciliation; the only child writer produced one coherent implementation and the probe child did not write /output.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source file; parent edits occurred after the child implementation returned.
The parent made targeted edits to existing source after joining child work, not a wholesale replacement of another live agent's non-entry source.
No live actor overwrote the required entry source or submitted artifact owned by another actor; final parent edits were sequential integration work.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another agent's final tree; the final artifact remained the integrated project.
Although the workspace was shared, only one child wrote implementation files and no unstable provenance or shared-write ambiguity materialized.
The probe child used /tmp scratch outputs only for reference observations, and no actor consumed another actor's temporary artifact as stable task input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The local background large-input command and its TaskStop were treated as one parent-owned verification/performance repair, not as child termination, blind waiting, or budget exhaustion.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no parallel-side adverse coordination pattern remained after parent integration and verification.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No label was retained for the successful use of a probe child, ordinary child implementation gaps later fixed by the parent, or serial-only coding defects.
